blocks.etymology: From Middle English woonted (“usual, customary”), from wont (“custom, habit, practice”), alteration of wone (“custom, habit, practice”), from Old English wuna (“custom, habit, practice; usual, wonted”), from Proto-Germanic *wunô (“custom, practice”), from Proto-Indo-European *wenh₁- (“to wish, love”). Cognate with Old Frisian wona, wuna (“custom”), Old High German giwona (“custom”). More at wont, wone.

thesaurus.definition: commonly used or practiced; usual

vi_block: Là thói thường (đối với ai), thông thường.

examples:
2008 (tr.?), Lodovico Ariosto, Orlando Furioso
But not with wonted welcome;—inly moved …
